title: Grok Bot Is Now a Model Router as SpaceX Continues to Pivot Further Toward AI Infrastructure
key_facts: Elon Musk, chief executive of SpaceX, announced on Twitter that the Grok Bot agent service will pick from several AI models for each request.
Models named: Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5, the Midjourney image generator and the Suno audio maker; SpaceX's own Grok 4.7 is presumably an option too.
Musk: simple questions go to small, fast models and complex ones to large models, choosing 'whatever is most likely to give you the best outcome'.
Gizmodo's own analysis: SpaceX could become infrastructure for other AI companies (renting out compute) rather than competing only on top models; this is not confirmed.
Background in the article: SpaceX agreed earlier this year to let Anthropic use its Colossus data center; Musk confirmed that Reflection AI's open model Beam was trained on Colossus servers.
The article says there is no sign that SpaceX will stop developing its own model.
quote_evidence: Per Musk, available models will include Anthropic’s Claude Opus 5.5, AI image generator MidJourney, AI audio maker Suno, and presumably others that weren’t named directly.
“Simple questions will route to small, fast models. Questions with complex answers will route to large models,” he explained.
why_it_matters_hint: Grok Bot users may get answers from other companies' models; the rule for choosing is not explained.
event_date: 6 Oct 2026 (Tuesday, per The Register's 7 Oct account; Gizmodo gives no date)
notes: Full article read. Trailing sidebar headlines on the page are not part of the story and were ignored. The headline's 'continues to pivot' is Gizmodo's reading; the body hedges it and so does the entry. Score lowered 6 to 5: event before 7 Oct (stale).
